School Vision
Our School
School Vision
Scargill Junior School believes that every child deserves the opportunity to learn, grow and achieve their full potential. Our ethos and vision are rooted in the personal qualities and values that guide every aspect of school life. As a school community, we promote and model respect for ourselves, for others and for our school.
We believe that clear boundaries, high expectations and positive relationships help children develop strong behaviours, resilience and ambition. By nurturing these qualities, we aim to equip our pupils with the skills, confidence and self-belief they need to succeed as they move on to the next stage of their education and lives.
At Scargill Junior School, we strive to create a safe, welcoming and inspiring environment where every child feels happy, valued and excited to learn. We are committed to providing opportunities for all pupils to thrive and succeed. Through a positive attitude, a commitment to learning and a relentless focus on personal growth and improvement, we encourage every child to strive for excellence.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Executive Head of School
A very warm welcome to our school website. You will find all of the key information about our school here. Our hope is that the website will provide a sense of what is important to our school and give you an insight into our approach to learning. At Scargill our motto is "Learning together, achieving together, succeeding together" which reflects our aim to work as one team for all to flourish.
It is a pleasure to welcome you and your child to our school. We hope that your time with us will be filled with happy memories, exciting opportunities and many achievements. Our dedicated team is committed to making sure every child feels valued, supported and inspired throughout their time with us
Our aim is simple, we want our pupils to leave us not only with a strong foundation for their future, but with a genuine love of learning, a belief in themselves and the confidence to make a positive difference in the world around them.
At the heart of our school are six values that shape who we are and how we treat one another:
These are much more than words. They are the qualities we seek to develop in every child, every day.
We teach our children to have Perseverance when learning is challenging, to show Respect and kindness towards others, and to have Aspiration — believing that their dreams and ambitions are worth pursuing. We encourage Independence, giving children the confidence to think for themselves, make positive choices and take responsibility for their learning. Through Sensitivity, we help our pupils understand and appreciate the feelings, experiences and perspectives of others. And with Enthusiasm, we encourage them to embrace every opportunity, approach life with curiosity and celebrate the joy of learning.
We believe that children flourish when they feel safe, happy and understood. Our dedicated staff work tirelessly to create a welcoming and inclusive environment in which every pupil can discover their strengths, overcome challenges and be proud of who they are.
Education is a partnership, and we greatly value the support of our parents and carers. By working together, we can give our children the very best possible start and help them develop into confident, compassionate and successful young people.
As you explore our website, I hope you get a sense of the energy, warmth and ambition that make our school such a special place. We are incredibly proud of our pupils, our staff and our wider school community.
Finally, we are always delighted to welcome prospective families to visit our school. A visit gives you the opportunity to see our school for yourself, experience our learning environment and meet the staff who are committed to providing the very best experiences for our children.

English
At Scargill Junior School we aim to develop children’s skills in English to help pupils unlock their potential across the curriculum and to develop a love of reading, writing and oracy. We have a well organised English curriculum that provides purposeful opportunities to achieve this.
Curriculum Intent
Subjects
Reading
Phonics
In line with the DFE and recognised best practice, we use a systematic synthetic phonics programmes (SSP). We have chosen to use Read, Write, Inc. (RWI). Any pupil identified as not yet being able to fully decode on entry to school, will be assessed and assigned to a RWI group.
Reading Comprehension
We teach comprehension as a whole class. Whole class reading enables teachers to take pupils beyond the 'cosy read' to the point of real challenge. The lessons are taught using a layered read approach.
Reading Independently
There is a time slot every day dedicated to independent reading. Each class has their own library and librarians where they can choose both a book at their reading level and a book of their own choice. Teachers listen to pupils read during this time. Pupils are also invited to write reviews of the books they have read.
Class Text
All teachers read to their class at least 4 times per week. This session is purely for enjoyment.
Book Club
The fifth session of the week is 'Book Club'. During this time, both the teacher and the pupils share recommendations of top reads. They will also sometimes get the opportunity to watch Mrs Graham's Book Club reviews on our school Youtube Channel.
Book Club on Youtube
Writing
At Scargill Junior School, our curriculum is structured around a selection of high quality, age-appropriate texts, enabling our pupils to develop and appreciate a rich and varied vocabulary from a range of authors. We use each text to create opportunities to develop links between reading and writing.
Teaching sequences allow children to explore different purposes for writing, key elements of genres and to explore good quality examples to scaffold their own written work. The pupils learn to evaluate the effectiveness of their writing by editing, redrafting and sharing their thoughts and opinions, fully supported by adults and their peers.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Right of Withdrawal from Religious Education - Scargill Junior School
pageCache.text:
The Right of Withdrawal from Religious Education
In England, parents and carers have the right to withdraw their children from Religious Education. This right of withdrawal exists for all pupils in all types of schools. Parents and carers also have the right to withdraw their child from part of RE and can do so without giving any explanation.
Religion and belief have become more visible in public life in recent years, making it important that all pupils should have an opportunity to engage in RE. However, the parent of a pupil may request that they be excused from all or part of the religious education (RE) provided.
Parents who wish to withdraw their children from RE should be aware of its aims and what is covered in the RE curriculum and that they are given the opportunity to discuss this if they wish. It should be made clear whether the withdrawal is from the whole RE curriculum or specific parts of it.
If you wish to withdraw your child from RE, or parts of RE, please contact our Executive Head of School Mr Tracey
Important – limitations to withdraw
If pupils are withdrawn from RE, schools have a duty to supervise them, though not to provide additional teaching. A pupil may be required to work in another area of the school, such as library or break out area.
Whilst parents or carers have a right to withdraw children from RE, they should note that children may also encounter religions and beliefs and wider aspects of faith in other areas of the curriculum from which there is no right of withdrawal.
On occasion, spontaneous questions about religious matters are raised by pupils or issues related to religion arise in other curriculum subjects such as history or citizenship (PSHE) For example, schools promote community cohesion and help pupils to understand ideas about identity and diversity, feelings and emotions within both religious and non-religious contexts.

Maths
At Scargill Junior School, we are committed to nurturing a deep and lasting understanding of mathematics in our pupils. Our curriculum is designed to ensure that students not only grasp mathematical concepts thoroughly but also develop fluency, reasoning, and problem-solving skills. We place a strong emphasis on the development of mathematical vocabulary and the ability to articulate and explain their thinking clearly. Through engaging and challenging lessons, we aim to foster a love of learning, encouraging curiosity and a positive attitude towards mathematics. By providing a supportive and inclusive environment, we prepare our students for future success in mathematics and other fields, equipping them with the confidence and skills to apply their knowledge in real-life contexts.
Mastery Approach
We are committed to embedding a Maths Mastery approach across our curriculum, aligning with the NCETM’s principles to ensure every pupil develops a deep, secure, and adaptable understanding of mathematics. This approach moves beyond rote learning, fostering a strong conceptual grasp that enables students to apply their mathematical knowledge in diverse contexts and solve problems creatively. Central to our practice is the belief that all pupils can learn and enjoy mathematics, promoting a positive attitude towards the subject. We focus on developing mathematical learning behaviours where pupils engage fully, reason logically, and seek to make connections between concepts. Our teachers continually enhance their specialist knowledge, collaborating to refine and improve their teaching strategies. The curriculum is designed with a coherent and detailed sequence of essential content, supporting sustained progression over time and ensuring that all pupils have the opportunity to master the concepts necessary for future success.
Maths No Problem
Our school is implementing the Maths — No Problem! scheme as a core part of our strategy to embed the mastery approach in mathematics teaching. This scheme is designed to support deep, long-term understanding by encouraging all pupils to move through content at the same pace, with an emphasis on problem-solving, reasoning, and conceptual understanding. Through the use of carefully structured lessons, visual representations, and collaborative learning, Maths — No Problem! aligns with the principles of mastery by ensuring that every child develops a secure and thorough grasp of mathematical concepts before progressing. This approach promotes confidence, resilience, and a love for mathematics across all year groups.
Times Tables Rock Stars
We actively promote the learning and recall of times tables through the use of TTRockstars, an engaging online platform designed to build speed and accuracy in multiplication and division facts. We recognise that secure knowledge of times tables forms the foundation for many areas of mathematics, and TTRockstars provides a fun and competitive environment that motivates pupils to practise regularly. Through individual challenges, class competitions, and school-wide events, we encourage all children to improve their fluency while developing a positive attitude towards maths. This consistent practice helps pupils build confidence and supports their overall mathematical progress.
